title: Lower-truncation reconstruction for quasi-coherent complexes on algebraic spaces
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$, with its small etale ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_X)$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $E\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] have quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with no boundedness assumption. For $n\in\mathbf N$ put $E_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$, let $c_n:E\to E_n$ and $f_n:E_{n+1}\to E_n$ be the canonical truncation maps [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. The product $P=\prod_{n\geq0}E_n$ exists in the ambient category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))$, and there is a distinguished triangle
$$E\xrightarrow{(c_n)_n}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\longrightarrow E[1],\qquad \operatorname{pr}_n s=f_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}.$$
Thus $E$, with these specified maps, is a derived limit of its lower-truncation tower [def-weil-derived-limit].

source.place: Tag 08F6, label lemma-nice-K-injective; canonical truncation reconstruction used at the start of the proof of Tag 08F7 (lemma-application-nice-K-injective), part (2).

proof.text: Choose the small skeleton allowed by [def-weil-size-convention] and let $\mathcal B$ consist of the affine scheme objects of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Every object $U\to X$ is covered by its affine open subschemes by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Their inclusions into $U$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and their composites with $U\to X$ are representable etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The inclusions are jointly surjective, hence form a covering in this site. This verifies the covering hypothesis of the site reconstruction theorem without any quasi-compactness or separation assumption on $X$.

source.place: Tag 08F6, label lemma-nice-K-injective, proof: the set of affine objects of the small etale site

proof.text: For a scheme object $u:U\to X$, postcomposition identifies $(X_{\mathrm{et}}/U,\mathcal O_X|_U)$ with $(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_U)$. Indeed an object on the left is a scheme map $V\to U$ whose composite with $u$ is etale; this map is etale by the final assertion of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Conversely an etale $V\to U$ has etale composite by its composition assertion. Arrows are precisely the same maps over $U$, coverings on both sides are jointly surjective etale families, and both rings evaluate on $V$ as $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For every $q$, the restriction $M_q=\mathcal H^q(E)|_U$ is quasi-coherent: the local presentations on the slice over each object are exactly those required by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], since relocalization identifies $(X_{\mathrm{et}}/U)/(V/U)$ with $X_{\mathrm{et}}/V$ and restriction of $\mathcal H^q(E)|_U$ along it with $\mathcal H^q(E)|_V$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tag 08F6, label lemma-nice-K-injective, proof; Tag 071Y, label section-higher-direct-image, scheme-object interpretation

proof.text: The module category on the small ringed site is Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice] to $\mathcal H^q(E)$ and the object $U$: for $p\geq0$ it identifies its module-derived evaluation $R^p\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},U}(\mathcal H^q(E))$, computed by injective module resolutions, with abelian cohomology on the slice, now $H^p(U_{\mathrm{et}},M_q)$. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] choose a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F_q$ on $U$ with $(F_q)_{\mathrm{et}}\cong M_q$. The isomorphisms of [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison] identify this group with $H^p(U,F_q)$. For affine $U$ the latter vanishes for every $p>0$ by [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing], applied to the affine open $U$ of itself. Thus $R^p\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},U}(\mathcal H^q(E))=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$, $p>0$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$. The site-reconstruction theorem of Step 4 defines $H^p(U,\mathcal H^q(E))$ by evaluating a K-injective resolution of $\mathcal H^q(E)[0]$; by [lem-sp-kinjective-computes](2), applied to the left exact additive evaluation $\Gamma(U,-)$ on the Grothendieck category of modules, an injective resolution is such a K-injective resolution and $H^p(U,\mathcal H^q(E))\cong R^p\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},U}(\mathcal H^q(E))$, and by (1) the choice of K-injective resolution does not matter. Hence $H^p(U,\mathcal H^q(E))=0$ in the convention needed below.

source.place: Tag 08F6, label lemma-nice-K-injective, proof: affine vanishing via Tag 071Y (spaces-cohomology.tex, section-higher-direct-image), Tag 03DW (descent.tex, proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent), and Tag 01XB (coherent.tex, lemma-quasi-coherent-affine-cohomology-zero)

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-site-truncation-derived-limit] to this small ringed site, the object $E$, the covering family of objects $\mathcal B$, and $d=0$. Step 3 supplies its vanishing hypothesis even for every $q$, so in particular for $q<0$. Its conclusion gives the existence of the ambient product and the distinguished triangle with first map $(c_n)_n$ and second map $1-s$ whose components are $f_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. By [def-kun-truncations] the good truncations used there have as images in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))$ the truncation functors of the standard t-structure; these are the very standard truncations and canonical maps of the item, so this is the asserted triangle, not merely an unspecified isomorphism of its first object with a derived limit.
